summary: In Greek mythology, Actor (Ancient Greek Ἄκτωρ, "leader") is an extremely common name. The atlas node actor-azeus is the Minyan ruler — son of Azeus, descendant of Phrixus — in whose palace at Orchomenus Astyoche conceives Ascalaphus and Ialmenus of Ares; those twins later lead the Minyan contingent to Troy.
etymology: From the verb ἄγω, "to lead or carry" — "leader."
symbols: Palace of the Minyan twins' begetting

sections.heading: Father of Astyoche
paragraphs: Homer and Pausanias place Actor son of Azeus as the Orchomenian whose daughter Astyoche bears the Minyan twin captains to Ares. He is a genealogical palace rather than a saga hero — the house in which the war-god's secret union produces Troy's Minyan leaders.

Homonym care is essential: not Actor father of Menoetius (Patroclus' grandfather); not Actor the Argonaut son of Hippasus (actor-argonaut); not Actor of Elis father of the Moliones; not Actor son of Deioneus. The atlas id is the Azeusid of Orchomenus alone.
